source:
Crea un juego completo de Roblox en 3D inspirado en la idea de "Escapa de Teclado", pero con mapas, mecánicas y modelos originales. No hagas un juego 2D. Debe ser una experiencia totalmente 3D con gráficos modernos y optimizada para PC y celular.

Concepto:
Los jugadores son personas miniatura atrapadas sobre un enorme escritorio. Deben escapar atravesando un teclado gigante mientras evitan obstáculos y peligros. El teclado debe sentirse enorme, con teclas gigantes que funcionan como plataformas.

Características:

- Mapa completamente 3D.
- Un teclado gigante como escenario principal.
- Varias zonas:
 - Teclas normales.
 - Teclas que desaparecen.
 - Teclas que rebotan.
 - Teclas que se hunden.
 - Zona del mouse.
 - Zona del monitor.
 - Zona de cables.
 - Zona del escritorio.
 - Zona de la CPU.
- Checkpoints automáticos.
- Sistema de guardado de progreso.
- Cronómetro para terminar el recorrido.
- Tabla de mejores tiempos (Leaderboard).
- Efectos de sonido al pisar teclas.
- Partículas en algunas zonas.
- Animaciones suaves.
- Música de fondo.
- Interfaz moderna.

Obstáculos:

- Láseres.
- Ventiladores.
- Teclas móviles.
- Plataformas giratorias.
- Cables eléctricos.
- Barras que empujan.
- Objetos que caen del escritorio.
- Zonas que eliminan al jugador.

Extras:

- Monedas coleccionables.
- Tienda de efectos cosméticos.
- Mascotas opcionales.
- Logros.
- Recompensas diarias.
- Sistema de niveles por experiencia.
- Botón para reiniciar desde el último checkpoint.

El estilo debe ser divertido, colorido y parecido a un obby moderno de Roblox, pero con identidad propia. Usa buenas prácticas, organiza correctamente el Explorer, separa Scripts, LocalScripts y ModuleScripts cuando sea necesario y evita código desordenado. El juego debe funcionar tanto en computadora como en dispositivos móviles.

answers.ask: How big is one key relative to the player - a single platform, or a whole area you walk around on?
answers.answer: Cada tecla debe ser una plataforma gigante individual, lo bastante grande para que un jugador miniatura se mueva sobre ella y salte entre teclas.

answers.ask: Are the nine zones one continuous route across the desk, or separate stages you teleport between?
answers.answer: Las nueve zonas forman una ruta continua sobre el mismo escritorio, sin teletransportes entre etapas.

answers.ask: Does the run end at the CPU, or somewhere else on the desk?
answers.answer: El recorrido termina en la zona de la CPU, que funciona como la meta final de escape.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: How big is one key relative to the player - a single platform, or a whole area you walk around on? A: Cada tecla debe ser una plataforma gigante individual, lo bastante grande para que un jugador miniatura se mueva sobre ella y salte entre teclas.
- [author] shape — Q: Are the nine zones one continuous route across the desk, or separate stages you teleport between? A: Las nueve zonas forman una ruta continua sobre el mismo escritorio, sin teletransportes entre etapas.
- [author] goal — Q: Does the run end at the CPU, or somewhere else on the desk? A: El recorrido termina en la zona de la CPU, que funciona como la meta final de escape.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a colorful modern 3D obby from the viewpoint of miniature people crossing one enormous desktop. Build one continuous route through exactly nine zones in order: normal keyboard keys, disappearing keys, bouncing keys, sinking keys, the mouse area, monitor area, cable area, open desktop area, and the CPU finish. Each giant key is an individual platform wide enough to move across before jumping to the next. Combine lasers, fans, moving keys, rotating platforms, electrical cables, pushing bars, falling desktop objects, and contact-lethal zones along the applicable sections. Keep every transition physically connected without teleports, use readable particles sparingly around special keys and hazards, and place the final escape area at the CPU. Compose the full desk as an oversized playful environment while preserving clear platform spacing and the miniature-player scale.

## Genre
The dominant and only genre is Obby & Platformer: player-controlled jumps, timed platforms, moving obstacles, checkpoints, and a terminal course define the experience.

## Shape and preset
Use `course-flat`, named Path (Flat Course), for a horizontal route crossing one desktop from the keyboard to the CPU. The matched preset is Classic Obby, expanded with the explicitly requested timed, lethal, collectible, and final-reward features.

## Config requirements
Use `path-track` for the physics-legal chain across all nine zones. Use `obstacle-jump` for giant-key gaps and bouncing keys, `obstacle-timing` for disappearing and sinking keys, and `obstacle-moving` for moving keys, rotating platforms, fans, pushing bars, and falling objects. Use `hazard-kill` for lasers, electrical cables, and elimination surfaces. Draw the safe-pad half of `checkpoint-respawn` at zone transitions and the visible finish half of `winner-zone` at the CPU.

## Layout requirements
Place nine `checkpoint-respawn` pads, one at the safe completion edge of each named zone, so a failure restarts at the latest cleared section. Scatter `collectible-nodes` coins along optional risky lines beside the safe route rather than directly on every mandatory landing. Place one `winner-zone` trigger at the CPU escape area, after the ninth zone. Progress saving, timing, leaderboard, cosmetics, pets, achievements, rewards, level systems, reset controls, audio, and UI are mechanics rather than additional map placements.

## Layout components
The single desktop map contains nine sequential zones connected without portals. The giant keyboard occupies the first four sections; mouse and monitor spaces form the middle; cables, open desk, and CPU form the final run. The course alternates stable key platforms with timed and moving hazards, then routes around large desk objects toward the CPU. Checkpoint pads divide the sections, coins sit on optional danger lines, and the CPU contains the terminal escape zone. Desk edges and lethal drops bound the course. Frame the start in the foreground and CPU in the background so the entire progression reads across one composition.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: establish the physics-legal continuous path, all nine ordered zones, safe landings, and checkpoint locations before dressing the isometric desktop. The top-down plan is authoritative because an impossible gap or disconnected section would make the obby unplayable.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is large, driven by one enormous desk containing nine zones while each individual key remains a traversable platform. The theme is colorful, playful modern desktop technology with smooth effects and an original obby identity. `P6` is mandatory for valid-by-construction platform spacing and course connectivity; no separate-map `P4` applies because the author requires one continuous desk.

options.text: A single continuous, physics-legal chain of platforms crossing the desktop through exactly nine ordered zones, with each giant key acting as its own traversable platform and all transitions physically connected (no teleports).
Jump gaps between oversized keys and bouncing-key sections that require discrete jumps at miniature-player scale.
Timed platforms in the disappearing-keys and sinking-keys zones (keys that vanish or drop after activation).
Moving keys and moving hazards including rotating platforms, fans, pushing bars, and falling desktop objects.
Contact-lethal hazards such as lasers, electrified cables, lethal drops off the desk edges, and elimination surfaces placed along applicable sections.
Safe landing pads at zone transitions that serve as respawn checkpoints so failure restarts at the latest cleared section.
A visible final escape area at the CPU that serves as the course end reward/finish.
Coins placed along optional risky lines beside the safe route, not on every mandatory landing.

layout_placement.text: Respawn checkpoint pads (safe landing pads) placed at the safe completion edge of each of the nine named zones, so a failure restarts at the latest cleared section.
layout_placement.where: One at the safe completion edge of each named zone transition.

layout_placement.text: One finish trigger at the CPU escape area, after the ninth zone.
layout_placement.where: At the CPU escape area, after the ninth zone.

layout_placement.text: Coins scattered along optional risky lines beside the safe route rather than directly on every mandatory landing.
layout_placement.where: Along optional risky lines beside the safe route (not on every mandatory landing).

layout.composition: Frame the start in the foreground and the CPU finish in the background so the entire progression reads across one composition, spanning the full desk from keyboard through mouse/monitor areas to cables, open desk, and CPU.

zones.name: normal keyboard keys
zones.role: Stable giant key platforms forming the start of the obby route.
zones.where: Start/foreground on the desktop, within the giant keyboard area.

zones.name: disappearing keys
zones.where: Immediately after normal keys, still on the giant keyboard.

zones.name: bouncing keys
zones.where: After disappearing keys, still on the giant keyboard.

zones.name: sinking keys
zones.where: After bouncing keys, still on the giant keyboard (end of the first four sections).

zones.name: mouse area
zones.role: Obstacle section routed through/around the mouse space as part of the continuous desk course.
zones.where: Middle of the desk route, after the keyboard sections.

zones.name: monitor area
zones.role: Obstacle section routed through/around the monitor space as part of the continuous desk course.
zones.where: Middle of the desk route, following the mouse area.

zones.name: cable area
zones.role: Hazard section featuring cables (including electrical cable hazards).
zones.where: Later in the route, after the monitor area.

zones.name: open desktop area
zones.role: Traversal section across open desk surface routing around large desk objects toward the CPU.
zones.where: Near the end of the route, before the CPU finish.

zones.name: CPU finish
zones.role: Terminal escape/finish area (winner zone) at the CPU.

layout.terrain: One enormous desktop surface used as the course base, with desk edges acting as lethal drops; hazards include lasers and electrical cables across applicable sections.
layout.boundary: Desk edges bound the course, with lethal drops/contact-lethal zones enforcing the boundary; no teleports/portals between sections.
layout.theme: Colorful, playful modern desktop technology obby at miniature-player scale with smooth effects.

render.why: An impossible gap or disconnected section would make the obby unplayable.

notes: Translated option `text` and `layout_placement.text` from Spanish/scene prose into English as required.
No explicit `paths` list (from/to/kind) was provided in the blob beyond the statement of one continuous route across nine zones, so `layout.paths` is empty rather than invented.
No explicit prop list with counts/placements was given as a props table; hazards/obstacles were captured via options instead, so `layout.props` is empty.
Option `winner-zone` is `goes_to=both`; it appears in `layout_placement` per the blob ('winner-zone trigger at the CPU'), and also in `options` with the visible finish geometry described.
